clue.text: Coin falling into one's hands in just seconds

indicators.note: only the second letter of each of the following words is taken, the 'seconds' of those words

explanation.surface: A coin drops into someone's open palms in a matter of moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in just seconds' reads as speed but asks for the second letters of falling, into, one's, hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a small unit of old Indian currency, a sixteenth of a rupee, and appears in crosswords as a coin.

clue.text: Accompany a POW unit after being shot

indicators.note: something shot to pieces is broken up, so these letters are blasted into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner-of-war unit is to escort someone once it has been fired upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after being shot' is the anagram signal on A POW UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait upon someone is to attend or escort them, an old courtly sense of accompanying a person.

clue.text: China provoke leader of Taiwan

parts.note: to tease is to needle or provoke someone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from Taiwan

explanation.surface: A political headline: China goads the head of Taiwan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country in the story but means porcelain crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain is called china, and a tea set is a matching group of cups and pot in that material.

clue.text: Monk is accommodating neckwear preferences

parts.note: a prior is a monk who heads a priory

indicators.note: the word is has room made inside it for another piece, so it holds that piece

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A monk keeps a stock of ties for others, according to their tastes.
explanation.definitionFit: Priorities are the things put first, so they reflect what one prefers or ranks highest.

clue.text: Our monarchy regularly airs main point about overseas theatre

indicators.note: turned about, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: the UK is a monarchy, ours from a British setter's point of view

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here the first and third of airs

parts.note: the nub is the central point of a matter

explanation.surface: The royal family routinely broadcasts the key issue concerning something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of airs; 'about' then turns the whole string round, so 'airs' and 'main point' are not the verb and phrase they seem.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunraku is the traditional Japanese puppet drama, a theatrical form from abroad.

clue.text: Purchaser's lower barn picked up

indicators.note: something picked up by the ear is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a lower is one that lows, a cow, and a byre is a cowshed

explanation.surface: A buyer has a cut-price barn noticed and snapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as cheaper but is a cow (it lows). BYRE is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is simply one who purchases, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Couldn't afford right move on time in Dundee ground

indicators.note: the following pieces are set inside the reworked letters
ground means crushed or broken up, so the letters of Dundee are reworked

parts.note: to budge is to shift slightly

explanation.surface: A football fan can't afford to switch allegiance at Dundee's stadium in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like Dundee's football stadium but is the anagram signal; 'in' puts the other pieces inside the jumbled city name, with 'on' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that is underbudgeted had too little money set aside, so it could not pay for what it needed.

clue.text: After polling, understands gains by Labour

indicators.note: to poll is to cut off the head, so the first letter is lopped off

parts.note: to learn is to come to understand

explanation.surface: An election-night pundit: once the votes are in, the Labour Party grasps its gains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polling' suggests voting but means beheading, removing the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain money through work, so earnings are what labour brings in.

clue.text: Want to stand in centre of Arsenal flag

indicators.note: one piece is placed to stand inside the other
the central letters of Arsenal are taken

parts.note: to want is to lack

explanation.surface: Someone wants to be in the middle of Arsenal's team, waving a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' at the end looks like a banner at the football match but is a verb, to tire. 'centre of' takes the middle three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or lose vigour, which is to slacken.

clue.text: Bully not retreating in, ultimately, fist fight

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the two final letters
the final letters of the following words are taken
going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: nary is a dialect word meaning not one

explanation.surface: A bully who won't back down in a punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' here is the dialect word nary, and 'retreating' reverses it; 'ultimately' applies to both fist and fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is an oppressive ruler or anyone who domineers over others, much as a bully does.

clue.text: Management face accepting concessions being rejected

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: dial is slang for a person's face

indicators.note: thrown back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: sops are small concessions made to appease

explanation.surface: Bosses confront workers by accepting that their concessions are turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rejected' reverses SOPS to SPOS, which DIAL takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something at your disposal means having control of it, so disposal is management or arrangement.

clue.text: Bohemian ideal of penniless sot?

definitions.meaning: an unconventional person living outside social norms
a broke drinker would most like spirits that cost nothing

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as free plus spirit, gin or whisky at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A free spirit is an independent, unconventional person, which is what a bohemian is.

clue.text: TV network's souvenir broadcast about moon

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the moon
scattered about, so the letters of souvenir are rearranged

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A TV channel's keepsake is aired, featuring the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' fits the TV surface but is the anagram signal; the moon is Jupiter's Io, which 'about' puts inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurovision is the European Broadcasting Union's programme exchange network, best known for its song contest.

clue.text: Black key — where E is found?

parts.note: in tells where something is

indicators.note: the E that is found in key is taken out of it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a black piano key and the note E.
explanation.walkthrough: E is found in the word key; lifting it out leaves IN KY, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means stained with or as dark as ink, so black.

clue.text: Stifling nostalgia — turn well away

indicators.note: well away suggests drunk and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nostalgia can be oppressive; best to turn well away from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well away' is the anagram signal on NOSTALGIA and TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangulation is choking someone by squeezing the throat, which is stifling them.

clue.text: Leaves trip with a lot of pain

parts.note: a spin is a short trip or drive

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Someone leaves on a journey in considerable discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departing but is the noun, foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a vegetable eaten for its leaves.

clue.text: Adult pages left on record — that is something fruity

parts.note: A is the film classification abbreviation for adult
an EP is an extended-play record
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Racy material left on a disc, which is rather juicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult' and 'fruity' suggest something saucy, but the pieces are plain abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple pie is a baked dessert filled with fruit.

clue.text: Port consumed by Frankie Vaughan

indicators.note: swallowed inside, so the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Port wine drunk by Frankie Vaughan, the 1950s crooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the drink in the singer's glass but means a harbour city. Frankie Vaughan was a British popular singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiev, now usually Kyiv, has a major river port on the Dnieper.

clue.text: Flagged police dog steps in

indicators.note: to police is to sort out and control, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A police dog moves in after being alerted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'police' reads as part of 'police dog' but is the anagram signal on DOG STEPS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To signpost something is to indicate it clearly, much as flagging it does.

clue.text: Beetle — vehicle crushed by wrecker

indicators.note: squeezed between, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: sab is short for saboteur, one who wrecks
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A beetle and a car are flattened by a demolition machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Penetrate chapter shunned by middle of America

indicators.note: kept out of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, middle

explanation.surface: A chapter of a society is cold-shouldered by the US heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of America' looks like a letter pick but is the American spelling of middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something is to go into it, which is to penetrate it.

clue.text: Trace short round handle for engine component

indicators.note: turned round, so the shortened word is reversed
cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a smack is a trace or slight flavour, as in a smack of garlic
a haft is the handle of a knife or tool

explanation.surface: Following a short trace around a handle to find a part of an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace' is a smack, as in a hint of flavour; 'short' drops its last letter and 'round' reverses what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is the rotating rod in an engine whose cams open and close the valves.

clue.text: In the City, finally leave union

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first
the last letters of the and City are taken

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: A City banker finally walks out of the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIT sits in E and Y, the last letters of 'the' and 'City'. Equity is the British actors' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the name of the performers' trade union in Britain.

clue.text: Preposition or noun covered by tuition off and on

indicators.note: the second piece sits inside the first
every other letter, off one and on the next

parts.note: N is the grammar abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson question: is it a preposition or a noun, covered in intermittent tutoring?
explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' takes U, T, O from tuition; N goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unto is an archaic word meaning to or towards, used as a preposition.

clue.text: House and well connected by a pipe

parts.note: OK means well, all right

explanation.surface: A house and a well linked by a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe' looks like plumbing but is a smoking pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooka, more often hookah, is an oriental tobacco pipe drawing smoke through water.

clue.text: Tramp's foot bandaged with towel?

indicators.note: wrapped round, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a towel is something that dries, a drier

explanation.surface: A vagrant's foot is wrapped up with a towel.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a person with no settled home who wanders about, a tramp.
